findings.title: Unescaped external JSON fields written into HTML response
findings.explanation: The /parser REST endpoint (registered in DemoApplication) fetches JSON over plain HTTP from api.flickr.com and streams the "farm", "server", "id" and "secret" field values directly into an HTML response via string concatenation (ps.println("")) with no HTML-encoding of any kind. Because the HTTP request to Flickr is unencrypted, any network-position attacker can tamper with the response (or Flickr's API could itself return unexpected content), injecting arbitrary HTML/JavaScript that is reflected verbatim to every browser that calls this endpoint, resulting in cross-site scripting.
